title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: You get a list of non-negative bar heights, each bar one unit wide. After rain, water collects in the dips between taller bars. Return the total units of water that stay trapped. Water at the outer edges runs off.

example.caption: Bars 3, 0, 2, 0, 4. The pits hold 3, 1 and 3 units, which is 7 in total.

output.label: 7 units of water. Green bars are filled up to the lower wall.

idea.sentence: Each bar holds water up to the lower of the tallest bar on its left and the tallest bar on its right. Two pointers find that level from both ends without storing it for every bar.

jargon.plain: min(tallest bar to the left, tallest bar to the right). Water cannot rise above the lower of the two.
The biggest value seen so far while scanning. It is updated in O(1) per step.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the bar heights, e.g. [3,0,2,0,4]

compare.bruteLabel: Scan both sides for every bar

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: For each bar, scan left and right to find the two tallest walls.

rows.name: Prefix arrays
rows.note: Precompute the left max and right max for every bar, then add up the water.

rows.name: Two pointers
rows.note: Only the two running maxima are kept. The lower side is finished first.

fast.takeaway: The arrays store the left max and right max for every bar. Two pointers notice that only the smaller of the two is ever needed, and keep just that.

stages.title: Both ends
stages.note: l and r at the ends. leftMax, rightMax and water all start at 0.

stages.title: Pick the lower side
stages.note: Compare the two bars. The lower side is safe to finish, because the other side already has a wall at least as tall.

stages.title: Add water
stages.note: Update that side's running max, add max minus bar height to the total, and move the pointer inward.

stages.title: Total
stages.note: When the pointers meet, every bar has been counted. Return the total.

stages.title: Left maxima
stages.note: left[i] is the tallest bar from the start through i. One pass left to right.

stages.title: Right maxima
stages.note: right[i] is the tallest bar from i to the end. One pass right to left.

stages.title: Sum the water
stages.note: Bar i holds min(left[i], right[i]) minus its own height. Add these up.

stages.title: Total
stages.note: The running sum is the answer.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: r starts at -1 so the loop never runs. No bars, no water.

edges.title: No pit
edges.why: Water has nothing on the right to stop it. Each bar is its own left max, so nothing is added.

edges.title: Flat ground
edges.why: Equal bars hold nothing. Ties go to the right pointer and add zero.

edges.title: One deep pit
edges.why: The middle bar fills up to the lower wall, which is 3.

gotchas.text: Compare the two bars first, then update only that side's max. Using the other side's max here is the classic mistake, because it may be smaller than the real lid.
The water at a bar is never negative. Update the running max before subtracting, so max minus height is at least 0.
new Array(n) makes a sparse array of holes, not zeros. Fill every cell before you read it, as the prefix pass does. Reading a hole gives undefined, and Math.max with undefined is NaN.
make([]int, n) gives a zero-filled slice. That suits the prefix arrays, but the first cell must still be set to height[0], not left at 0, or the left max starts too low.
len(height) - 1 is -1 for an empty or nil slice. The loop condition l < r stops that, so no special case is needed.

recap.key: A bar holds min(left max, right max) minus its height. Finish the lower side first, since its limit is already known.
moves: l and r at the ends, maxima at 0
Pick the side with the lower bar
Update its max, add max minus bar height
Move that pointer inward until they meet
